name: Addendum A1 to protocol_baselines.json (sha256 d0ec4b6b2f5ba152a852b28d5372078c3891c73113224c5ac54f92447948c479)
written: 2026-11-09, after the primary BACC-r, ACI and ACI-G test results and one post hoc BACC-r variant without the change limit had been seen; before any run listed here
source_pinned: BACC as described in arXiv:2606.20575v2 (13 October 2026); no public code at the time of writing; the comparator is called BACC-r (our re-implementation of the v2 description), not BACC
purpose: sensitivity of BACC-r to the details the v2 text leaves unspecified or that depend on the scale of its own experiments; all variants are reported
primary_unchanged: BACC-r primary = c = mu, max change 100 capacity units per decision, A_k summed over all minutes with plans, trigger on, h = 5

variants.V3_no_limit: no limit on the change per decision (in the v2 experiments, with 3-77 replicas, the 100-replica limit rarely binds)
variants.V4_hpa_limit: scale-up per decision at most max(4, planned count) (HPA default policy), scale-down unlimited
variants.V5_A_missed: alternative reading of Step 3: A_k summed only over minutes whose demand exceeded the calibrated demand of the plan in force
variants.V6_no_trigger: budget-aware trigger off (the paper's own ablation removes it)

cells: three traces x delta in {0.01, 0.05} x tau in {0, 1, 5}; same environment, forecasts and cost as the primary protocol
robustness_criterion: per trace at the primary cell (tau=1, delta=0.01), the comparison with PAC-h is called robust if, in every variant, BACC-r keeps no more units within budget than PAC-h, or, where it keeps more, its median per-unit cost ratio to PAC-h over units where both comply is above 1; otherwise the variant that reverses the comparison is reported as such
aci_diagnostics: no new ACI configuration; for the already selected ACI-G and for ACI, report per-unit ACI miscoverage (err fraction) and overload minutes outside saturated minutes, to check that the finite-horizon bound holds as implemented
not_done: no AutoARIMA forecaster (not available offline in this environment); persistence for every controller, as before
